meta.title: Business Structures for Foreign Investors — Saudi Arabia
meta.description: Structured reference data on the main legal entity types available to foreign investors in Saudi Arabia. Covers characteristics, use cases, and MISA licensing requirements. Contains placeholder fields where official verification is still required.
meta.last_verified: [PLACEHOLDER — add ISO date YYYY-MM-DD when content is verified against current official sources]
meta.disclaimer: This dataset is for general educational and informational purposes only. It is not legal, financial, or regulatory advice. Requirements are subject to change. Always verify with official Saudi government sources and qualified professionals before making decisions.

data.name: Limited Liability Company
data.short_description: The most commonly used structure for foreign investors establishing an operating presence in Saudi Arabia. Partners' liability is generally limited to their capital contribution. Can be established with a single shareholder or multiple partners.

ownership_type.notes: Full foreign ownership is permitted in many sectors under Vision 2030 reforms. Certain sectors may still require a local partner or remain restricted. Eligibility is determined by MISA's approved activity list.

legal_entity_status.notes: The LLC is a distinct legal entity from its partners. Partners are generally not personally liable beyond their agreed capital contribution.

requires_misa_license.notes: Foreign investors must obtain a MISA investment registration before registering commercially. The registration is activity-specific. Local (Saudi/GCC) investors register directly with the Ministry of Commerce without a MISA registration. ⚠️ ELIGIBILITY (verified: MISA Investor Guide 12th Ed., March 2025, §3.1.1): Standard MISA Investment Registration requires (1) commercial registration of the applicant's foreign establishment authenticated by the Saudi Embassy, and (2) audited financial statements for the last fiscal year. Foreign individuals WITHOUT an established foreign company (minimum 1 year of operation) do NOT qualify for standard registration. Available paths for individuals: (a) Has established foreign company (1+ year, CR + audited financials authenticated) → standard path; (b) Holds Saudi Premium Residency → documents waived; (c) Innovative/tech business with MISA-recognized VC/incubator support letter → Entrepreneurial Registration only. GCC nationals may register directly with the Ministry of Commerce without a MISA registration.

registration_body.notes: Commercial Registration (CR) is issued by the Ministry of Commerce after MISA registration approval for foreign investors.

official_sources.name: Ministry of Investment (MISA)
official_sources.role: Investment registration issuance and sector eligibility

data.verification_method: Reviewed the Companies Law (Royal Decree No. M/132, 2022), official English translation by the Bureau of Experts at the Council of Ministers, obtained from misa.gov.sa, on 2026-06-14. Confirmed the LLC formation and capital provisions (Arts. 156, 157, 174). Sector-level foreign-ownership eligibility (a dynamic MISA activity list) remains open — see placeholders.

field_verifications.value_summary: An LLC is incorporated by one or more natural or legal persons; a single-person LLC is permitted; the Law sets no maximum number of partners.
field_verifications.source: Companies Law, Royal Decree No. M/132 (2022), official English translation by the Bureau of Experts at the Council of Ministers (misa.gov.sa)
field_verifications.citation: Art. 156: 'A limited liability company is a company incorporated by one or more natural or legal persons.' Art. 157(1): 'The incorporation of a limited liability company by a single person or the transfer of all of its interests to a single person shall entail the following: ...'

field_verifications.value_summary: No statutory minimum capital for an LLC; partners determine the company's capital in the articles of incorporation.
field_verifications.source: Companies Law, Royal Decree No. M/132 (2022), official English translation by the Bureau of Experts at the Council of Ministers (misa.gov.sa)
field_verifications.citation: Art. 174: 'Partners shall determine the capital of the company in its articles of incorporation. Such capital shall be divided into indivisible and untradeable interests of equal value.'

placeholders.description: The specific list of sectors open to 100% foreign LLC ownership is governed by MISA's approved activities list and may be updated. Verify current sector eligibility before proceeding.

data.name: Joint Stock Company
data.short_description: A more complex corporate structure suited to larger enterprises, heavily regulated sectors, or businesses intending to raise public capital or list on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul). Subject to more rigorous governance requirements than an LLC.

ownership_type.notes: Foreign ownership is possible but subject to MISA registration and sector-specific rules. Some regulated sectors may impose foreign ownership caps regardless of structure.

legal_entity_status.notes: Shareholders' liability is limited to the value of their shares. The JSC is a fully distinct legal entity.

typical_use_cases: Large-scale enterprises requiring complex capital structures
Regulated industries such as banking, insurance, and telecoms
Companies seeking listing on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul)
Businesses requiring broad public or institutional shareholding
Entities seeking access to Saudi capital markets

requires_misa_license.notes: Foreign investors must obtain a MISA investment registration. For listed JSCs, additional requirements from the Capital Market Authority (CMA) apply.

registration_body.notes: JSCs must also comply with CMA regulations if they intend to offer shares publicly or list on Tadawul.

official_sources.name: Capital Market Authority (CMA)
official_sources.role: Regulation of listed and public JSCs

data.verification_method: Reviewed the Companies Law (Royal Decree No. M/132, 2022), official English translation by the Bureau of Experts at the Council of Ministers, obtained from misa.gov.sa, on 2026-06-14. Confirmed JSC formation and minimum capital (Arts. 58, 59). Board composition (Art. 67) and AGM cadence (Art. 88) are confirmed but the audit committee / CMA Corporate Governance Regulations requirement for listed JSCs remains open — see placeholders.

field_verifications.value_summary: A JSC is incorporated by one or more natural or legal persons; a single-shareholder JSC is permitted.
field_verifications.source: Companies Law, Royal Decree No. M/132 (2022), official English translation by the Bureau of Experts at the Council of Ministers (misa.gov.sa)
field_verifications.citation: Art. 58: 'A joint-stock company is a company incorporated by one, or more, natural or legal persons and its capital is divided into tradable shares. ... The liability of shareholders shall be limited to paying the value of the subscribed shares.'

field_verifications.value_summary: Minimum issued capital is SAR 500,000; at least one quarter is paid up on incorporation.
field_verifications.source: Companies Law, Royal Decree No. M/132 (2022), official English translation by the Bureau of Experts at the Council of Ministers (misa.gov.sa)
field_verifications.citation: Art. 59: 'The issued capital of a joint-stock company shall not be less than five hundred thousand riyals and its paid-up capital upon incorporation shall not be less than a quarter of said capital.'

placeholders.description: Board composition and AGM cadence are confirmed in the Companies Law (board of at least three members, Art. 67; ordinary general assembly annual meeting within six months of fiscal year-end, Art. 88). The remaining unverified element is the audit committee requirement and other CMA Corporate Governance Regulations obligations applicable to listed JSCs, which could not be confirmed against the live CMA regulation text.

data.name: Branch of a Foreign Company
data.short_description: An extension of a foreign parent company operating in Saudi Arabia. Not a separate legal entity — the parent company bears full legal and financial responsibility for all of the branch's activities in the Kingdom.

ownership_type.notes: A branch is by definition an extension of a foreign parent entity. Ownership cannot be transferred to a local partner without converting to a different structure.

legal_entity_status.notes: The branch has no independent legal existence from its parent. All obligations, liabilities, and contracts are those of the foreign parent company.

typical_use_cases: Operating directly under the foreign parent brand and entity name
Companies preferring the parent to retain full legal control
Project-based or contract-driven operations in Saudi Arabia
Businesses not seeking permanent local incorporation

requires_misa_license.notes: A MISA investment registration is required before a foreign company branch can be registered with the Ministry of Commerce.

registration_body.notes: The branch receives its own Commercial Registration (CR) number even though it is not a separate legal entity.

official_sources.name: Ministry of Investment (MISA)
official_sources.role: Investment registration for foreign company branch

placeholders.description: Whether a branch's permitted activities must exactly mirror those of the parent company or can differ. Verify with MISA.
Specific documents required from the parent company (e.g., notarized board resolution, parent financial statements, apostille requirements) for branch registration.

data.name: Representative Office
data.short_description: A non-commercial presence linked to a foreign parent company, permitted only for promotional, research, or liaison activities. Cannot engage in direct commercial transactions, sign commercial contracts on its own behalf, or generate revenue in Saudi Arabia.

ownership_type.notes: A representative office is directly linked to and dependent on a foreign parent company. It has no independent ownership structure.

legal_entity_status.notes: The representative office is not a standalone legal entity. It operates as a presence of the foreign parent and cannot independently hold assets, contracts, or liabilities.

typical_use_cases: Coordinating parent company activities and relationships in Saudi Arabia
Initial market entry before committing to a full commercial structure

requires_misa_license.notes: A MISA registration is required for a representative office. The registration type may differ from that issued for commercial entities. The office's permitted activities are defined by the registration.

registration_body.notes: Registration requirements and whether Ministry of Commerce registration is also required should be verified with MISA directly.

official_sources.name: Ministry of Investment (MISA)
official_sources.role: Representative office registration and permitted activities

placeholders.description: The specific MISA registration category applicable to a representative office and how it differs from a commercial entity registration. Verify with MISA.
The exact scope of activities a representative office may perform (e.g., whether it may sign contracts on behalf of the parent, hire Saudi staff, or lease office space).
Whether a representative office license has a fixed term, renewal requirements, or conditions for conversion to a commercial structure.
